hot.title: Looped World Models
hot.summary: LoopWM introduces the first looped transformer architecture for world modeling, leveraging iterative latent depth to achieve stable long-horizon simulations with high parameter efficiency. The model demonstrates superior predictive accuracy and reduced computational cost on benchmarks like ScienceWorld and AlfWorld, outperforming models up to 100 times larger.

hot.title: Reversal Q-Learning
hot.summary: Reversal Q-Learning (RQL) introduces an off-policy reinforcement learning algorithm that trains expressive flow policies from static datasets by utilizing a novel flow reversal technique to construct virtual trajectories within an expanded Markov Decision Process. The method mitigates training instability and the curse of horizon, achieving the highest average performance across 50 simulated robotic manipulation and locomotion tasks in the OGBench benchmark.

hot.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
hot.summary: S-AGENT introduces a framework for spatial intelligence in Vision-Language Models, enabling them to reason over continuous, evolving 3D environments by accumulating spatio-temporal evidence. This is achieved through a VLM planner orchestrating hierarchical spatial tools and dual memory systems, leading to improved performance on multi-image and video spatial reasoning benchmarks.

hot.title: Variable-Width Transformers
Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos
hot.summary: The DO AS I DO algorithm generates dexterous manipulation data for multi-fingered robots by reconstructing 3D hand-object interactions from everyday monocular human videos and retargeting them into executable robot actions. This approach achieved a 71% success rate on reconstructed in-the-wild trajectories and demonstrated real-world execution across diverse tasks.

hot.title: MemoryWAM: Efficient World Action Modeling with Persistent Memory
hot.summary: A hybrid memory design is presented for World Action Models, enabling efficient and persistent long-range context for robotic manipulation in memory-dependent tasks. This approach achieves comparable or superior performance to full-history models on benchmarks like RMBench and real-world scenarios while significantly reducing inference latency and GPU memory consumption.

hot.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
ImageWAM: Do World Action Models Really Need Video Generation, or Just Image Editing?
hot.summary: ImageWAM reconfigures pretrained image editing models to act as efficient visual backbones for robot action prediction, demonstrating that compact, instruction-conditioned visual transformation representations can replace full video generation in World Action Models. This approach achieved up to 93.56% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 83.1% on LIBERO-Plus, while reducing inference latency by approximately 75% and computational FLOPs by about 83% compared to video-generation WAMs.

hot.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
hot.summary: A multi-agent Code-as-Policy system, RATS, enables robots to autonomously acquire reusable skills through self-directed play. The system improved average task success rates by 20.6 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO and 17.0 percentage points on MolmoSpaces, and demonstrated effective sim-to-real and cross-environment skill transfer.

hot.title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
hot.summary: Engels et al. (2026) investigate the transparency of DiffusionGemma, a text diffusion model, finding it achieves comparable monitorability to autoregressive models like Gemma 4. The study demonstrates that its latent intermediate states can be made largely interpretable, significantly reducing its 'opaque serial depth' and revealing unique non-autoregressive reasoning patterns.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotManip Technical Report: Alignment Unlocks Scale for Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotManip, a Vision-Language-Action foundation model, demonstrates that aligning heterogeneous robotic data enables effective data scaling and emergent generalization capabilities for manipulation tasks. The model achieves robust performance across various out-of-distribution scenarios and real-world deployments by integrating a unified cross-embodiment formulation and a large-scale open-source pretraining corpus.

hot.title: SC3-Eval: Evaluating Robot Foundation Models via Self-Consistent Video Generation
hot.summary: SC3-Eval introduces a self-consistent video generation framework for evaluating generalist robot manipulation policies, adapting a unified dynamics model to enforce multiple forms of consistency. This approach achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.984 and an MMRV of 0.022 for in-distribution online evaluation, also demonstrating enhanced reproduction of policy failure modes.

hot.title: Learning from the Self-future: On-policy Self-distillation for dLLMs
hot.summary: d-OPSD introduces the first on-policy self-distillation framework tailored for diffusion large language models, leveraging 'self future-experience' and step-level divergence supervision to enable self-improvement. The framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in reasoning tasks while demonstrating superior sample efficiency, converging in approximately 10% of the optimization steps required by RLVR methods.

hot.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
hot.summary: WRBench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating video generation models, reveals that current systems struggle to maintain a consistently evolving world state independent of observation. It exposes a "preservation–access–re-observed-consistency gap," where models often fail to correctly advance object states and events when out of view, performing as "tracking shots" instead of genuine world models.

hot.title: VibeThinker-3B: Exploring the Frontier of Verifiable Reasoning in Small Language Models
hot.summary: VibeThinker-3B, a 3-billion-parameter model from Sina Weibo Inc., achieves advanced verifiable reasoning capabilities, matching or exceeding the performance of significantly larger language models on demanding benchmarks in mathematics, coding, and scientific reasoning. The model scored 94.3 on AIME26 and 80.2 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6, further improving to 97.1 on AIME26 and 99.2 on BruMO25 with Claim-Level Reliability Assessment.

hot.title: AtomMem: Building Simple and Effective Memory System for LLM Agents via Atomic Facts
hot.summary: Researchers from the University of Science and Technology of China developed AtomMem, a long-term memory system for LLM agents that extracts and organizes atomic facts hierarchically with graph-based associative recall. The system achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks like LoCoMo, demonstrating improved complex reasoning and reducing API token consumption by approximately 61.4%.

hot.title: Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System
hot.summary: Qwen-RobotNav presents a scalable, reconfigurable navigation model for embodied agent systems, building on a vision-language foundation to dynamically adapt its observation strategy at inference time. The model achieves state-of-the-art results across various navigation benchmarks and substantially improves Embodied Question Answering performance by enabling external control over visual context.

hot.title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
hot.summary: Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM), developed by researchers at ELLIS Institute Tübingen and ETH Zurich, present a looped transformer architecture designed for stable and adaptive reasoning. The model incorporates a fixed-point convergence mechanism for intrinsic halting and utilizes pre-normalization with residual scaling to manage signal propagation in deep effective layers, achieving competitive or superior performance on various puzzle tasks while adaptively allocating computation based on task complexity.

hot.title: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
hot.summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory researchers developed Self-Harness, a paradigm allowing a fixed Large Language Model (LLM) agent to autonomously improve its own operating harness by iteratively diagnosing weaknesses, proposing minimal modifications, and validating them. This method achieved significant performance improvements on the Terminal-Bench-2.0 benchmark across various LLMs, demonstrating the generation of targeted, model-specific harness configurations.

hot.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
hot.summary: A study empirically compares egocentric human video and real-robot data for embodied pretraining, demonstrating that human video yields superior generalization to unseen tasks and enhanced robustness in real-world robot deployment, even with pseudo-action labels. The research finds that egocentric data scales predictably and fosters a more effective "open-world prior" for robotic policies.

likes.title: GLM-5.2: Built for Long-Horizon Tasks
You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences
likes.summary: Researchers from UIUC and NYU propose Temporal Difference in Vision (TDV), a self-supervised method for learning visual representations from video by predicting future frame embeddings from past frames and learned motion. This approach, which avoids strong inductive biases, demonstrates improved performance on dense spatial tasks like optical flow and stereo depth compared to existing techniques like DINO and iBOT.

likes.title: Qwen-RobotWorld Technical Report: Unifying Embodied World Modeling through Language-Conditioned Video Generation
likes.summary: Qwen-RobotWorld introduces a language-conditioned video world model from the Qwen Team that unifies various embodied domains, including manipulation, driving, and navigation, using natural language as a singular action interface. The model predicts physically plausible future visual trajectories and demonstrates top performance on embodied intelligence benchmarks like EWMBench and DreamGen Bench.

likes.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction
likes.summary: The Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington developed MolmoMotion, a system that forecasts object-attached 3D point trajectories in world coordinates, conditioned on language instructions and visual history. This method improved robot manipulation task success rates by over 20 percentage points and enhanced video generation realism, outperforming existing motion prediction baselines on a new 3D motion benchmark.

likes.title: Variable-Width Transformers
DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model
likes.summary: The DreamX Team developed DreamX-World 1.0, a general-purpose interactive world model that transitions video generation from passive synthesis to dynamic, user-controlled simulation. This model achieved the highest overall scores in basic (84.76) and long-horizon (70.41) evaluations against larger competitors, and was preferred by humans in 57.5-61.9% of cases, while also demonstrating enhanced scene persistence and real-time streaming at up to 16 FPS.

likes.title: Unsafe AI or Consolidated Power: AI’s False Dichotomy
Geometric Action Model for Robot Policy Learning
likes.summary: The Geometric Action Model (GAM) repurposes a pretrained Geometric Foundation Model (GFM) as a unified backbone for language-conditioned robot manipulation, integrating 3D perception, future geometry prediction, and action decoding. This approach improves policy robustness to environmental changes and achieves significantly faster inference speeds, up to 55 times quicker than diffusion-based baselines.

likes.title: Latent Thought Flow: Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
likes.summary: Latent Thought Flow (LTF), developed by researchers at Singapore Management University and Ant Group, enables Large Language Models to perform adaptive, efficient multi-step reasoning directly within their continuous latent space. The framework, which leverages GFlowNets, achieved an average accuracy improvement of 9.5% and a 27.2% reduction in reasoning length compared to existing latent reasoning methods across various LLM backbones and benchmarks.

likes.title: ExpRL: Exploratory RL for LLM Mid-Training
likes.summary: ExpRL, developed by researchers from Stanford University, Carnegie Mellon University, and OpenAI, introduces an on-policy reinforcement learning approach for mid-training large language models by using human-written reference solutions as dense reward scaffolds. This method improves the initial policy for subsequent sparse-reward RL, leading to enhanced reasoning capabilities and achieving 63.41% pass@1 on AIME-2026 after downstream training, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and sparse reward baselines.

likes.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley, NVIDIA, Stanford, and other institutions developed the T-Rex framework, enabling Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to incorporate high-frequency tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation. This approach achieved an average success rate of 65% across 12 contact-rich tasks, outperforming the strongest baseline by more than 30%.

likes.title: LaWAM: Latent World Action Models for Efficient Dynamics-Aware Robot Policies
likes.summary: LaWAM (Latent World Action Models) proposes an approach for dynamics-aware robot policies that efficiently predict compact latent visual subgoals, rather than high-dimensional pixel-level future observations. This method enables robots to anticipate action consequences with significantly reduced inference latency and model complexity compared to traditional pixel-space world models, achieving high success rates across diverse manipulation tasks.
